claims.claim: In 11,530 UK Biobank participants, each +1 mL/kg/min/year of estimated VO2max was associated with a hazard ratio of 0.85 for incident cardiovascular disease and 0.66 for cardiovascular death.
claims.episode_span: Each additional 1 mL·kg−1·min−1·year−1 of estimated VO2max was associated with a hazard ratio of 0.85 for incident disease (0.75 to 0.96) and 0.66 for cardiovascular death (0.51 to 0.87).
claims.source_title: Longitudinal changes of cardiorespiratory fitness are associated with cardiovascular disease and mortality
claims.supporting_quote: Annual improvements in VO₂max were associated with a lower risk of incident CVD [hazard ratio (HR) per +1 mL·kg-1·min-1·year-1 = 0.85; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.75-0.96] and CVD-related mortality (HR = 0.66, 95% CI 0.51-0.87).
